tema: Evaluates whether CPET-defined deconditioning explains orthostatic intolerance in ME/CFS.
diseno: Study with 22 healthy controls and 199 ME/CFS patients; classification of deconditioning by % peak VO2 on CPET and CBF reduction during the tilt test; normal haemodynamic response, POTS or orthostatic hypotension.
hallazgos: Controls had higher oxygen consumption and less CBF reduction than patients, but there were no differences in CBF reduction between patients with no, mild or severe deconditioning, nor between the three haemodynamic patterns.
conclusion: OI in ME/CFS is not caused by deconditioning; the abnormal CBF reduction was present regardless of % peak VO2.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent and reinforce that deconditioning does not explain OI; the conclusions frame it as a refutation of a widespread opinion.

tema: Analyses whether PEM is a unitary construct or is composed of generalized fatigue and specific muscle fatigue.
diseno: Exploratory factor analysis of PEM symptoms in an international convenience sample with self-reported diagnosis; size not stated.
hallazgos: PEM is composed of two empirically distinct experiences: one of generalized fatigue and one of specific muscle fatigue.
conclusion: PEM is not a single construct but a two-dimensional one; future studies must confirm it in more homogeneous populations with standardized diagnostic criteria.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on construct validity. The conclusions come from the discussion and focus on limitations (self-reported diagnosis, Caucasian and multinational sample), without reaffirming the central finding.

tema: Studies DMN connectivity and complexity in CFS to understand its pathophysiology and identify biomarkers.
diseno: High temporal resolution fMRI in 72 subjects (45 with CFS and 27 controls) at rest and during a task; static and dynamic connectivity, BOLD maps and complexity; general linear model and hierarchical regression.
hallazgos: The BOLD signal of the posterior cingulate cortex was more complex in CFS; connectivity between the medial prefrontal cortex and inferior parietal lobes was weaker, and dynamic connectivity more complex during the task. Each difference explained 7-11% of the variability in health scores.
conclusion: The DMN is more irregular and less coordinated in CFS; these deficits could be energetically costly and contribute to fatigue, cognitive symptoms and PEM, and could serve as a biomarker.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the DMN and its hubs; the conclusions (from the discussion, with editorial noise) add the energy-cost hypothesis and the link with PEM.

tema: Analyses muscle oxygen extraction and the cardiac output/oxygen consumption relationship during CPET in CFS.
diseno: Retrospective CPET study with continuous non-invasive measurement of cardiac output (Nexfin) in patients with CFS (178 women, 25 men), idiopathic chronic fatigue (172 and 51) and healthy individuals (11 and 7).
hallazgos: Peak oxygen extraction was lower in CFS than in idiopathic fatigue and healthy individuals in both sexes; the ΔQ/ΔVO2 ratio was above 6 L/L in 70% of patients versus 22% of healthy individuals.
conclusion: Low muscle oxygen uptake causes exercise intolerance in most CFS patients, indicating insufficient metabolic adaptation; the high increase in cardiac output argues against deconditioning.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on the metabolic cause. The PDF conclusions are somewhat more cautious, speaking of consistency with a metabolic cause in 70% in a retrospective study.

tema: Deep phenotyping of ME/CFS in a Japanese population to identify molecular markers.
diseno: Case-control with 48 patients and 52 controls; laboratory analysis, plasma metabolomics, immunophenotyping, transcriptomics and faecal microbiome.
hallazgos: 26 potential markers distinguished patients; monocyte count, microbiome and lipoproteins were the most informative; lipoproteins and microbiome correlated with sleep disturbance.
conclusion: A cluster of sleep-related molecular changes is a prominent feature in this cohort.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract consistent; the conclusions text is statistical-methods noise, with no useful comparison.

tema: Multi-omic analysis of the gut microbiome and its butyrate-producing capacity in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control with 106 patients and 91 controls from various regions; metagenomics, qPCR, faecal SCFA metabolomics, co-abundance networks and machine learning classifiers.
hallazgos: Reduction of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Eubacterium rectale and deficient butyrate synthesis; F. prausnitzii inversely associated with fatigue severity; classifiers robust in validation.
conclusion: The dysbiosis is functional and offers targets for classification and therapeutic trials.
triangulacion: Full coherence among the three sources (butyrate, F. prausnitzii, SCFA); the conclusions include methods noise.

tema: To measure serum BH4 in ME/CFS with orthostatic intolerance and small fibre polyneuropathy.
diseno: Pilot study: BH4 ELISA in serum of 32 patients with CFS, 10 with CFS + OI and 12 with CFS + OI + SFN versus controls; ROS assay in microglia.
hallazgos: BH4 significantly elevated in the three groups versus controls; association with oxidative stress response.
conclusion: Regulation of BH4 metabolism could be a target for understanding the mechanism of CFS and of CFS with OI.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract consistent; the conclusions text is administrative noise and does not allow comparison.

tema: To identify urinary metabolites before and after exercise in a rat model of CFS.
diseno: Animal experimental study: model induced over 4 weeks by restraint stress, forced exercise and a noisy environment; urinary GC-MS with multivariate analysis.
hallazgos: 20 metabolites detected; alterations in the TCA cycle, alanine-aspartate-glutamate metabolism and steroid hormone biosynthesis; sphingolipids altered only after exercise.
conclusion: Sphingosine and 21-hydroxypregnenolone could be biomarkers, in relation to immune dysfunction and HPA axis hypoactivity.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions are more cautious in warning that the animal model differs from patients.

tema: To review alterations of creatine metabolism and supplementation trials in post-viral fatigue syndrome.
diseno: Critical review of creatine alterations in PVFS populations and human trials with creatine and analogues.
hallazgos: Alterations are described in brain creatine, muscle phosphocreatine resynthesis and serum creatine kinase; supplements appear to influence outcomes.
conclusion: There is insufficient evidence to support creatine, but the initial results justify investigating it, also in post-COVID-19 fatigue.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions are more cautious than the abstract and add the post-COVID perspective.

tema: Evaluates the diagnostic sensitivity of the two-day CPET and looks for cut-off points to distinguish ME/CFS from controls.
diseno: Case-control study with 16 ME/CFS patients and 10 healthy controls; cycle ergometer CPET on two consecutive days; ROC analysis.
hallazgos: Workload at the ventilatory threshold decreased from day 1 to day 2 by a greater magnitude in ME/CFS; decreases of 6.3% to 9.8% offered optimal sensitivity and specificity. There was no interaction in other parameters.
conclusion: A 6.3-9.8% decrease in workload at the ventilatory threshold on the second day could be an objective biomarker to support the diagnosis of ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent. The conclusions add that the decrease was not accompanied by changes in peak HR or peak VO2, reinforcing that it is not due to lower effort; the sample is small.

tema: Compares PEM symptoms and disease characteristics between ME and CFS patients with normal and abnormal exercise test results.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with an international convenience sample with self-reported diagnosis and self-reported exercise test results; size not stated.
hallazgos: Those with abnormal results had more frequent and severe PEM, worse overall functioning and a higher probability of being bedbound.
conclusion: The most severe patients may be excluded from exercise studies, which could hide differences from controls; controlled and standardized studies are required.
triangulacion: Abstract and keywords are consistent. The conclusions (from the discussion) focus on selection bias and on limitations (self-report, unknown type of test), more cautious than the abstract.

tema: Determines whether ME/CFS is an extreme form of fatigue or a qualitatively distinct condition by comparing its risk factors with those of severe fatigue.
diseno: Prospective cohort of US nurses (n = 41,802; 102 with ME/CFS, 522 with severe fatigue) followed since 1989; mailed questionnaire and Cox proportional hazards regression.
hallazgos: Severe fatigue was associated with older age, high BMI, hormone therapy, higher alcohol consumption and lower caffeine intake, associations absent in ME/CFS. Prior infectious mononucleosis was non-significantly associated with ME/CFS (HR 1.77; 0.87-3.61) and to a lesser extent with severe fatigue (HR 1.28).
conclusion: The different risk factors suggest that ME/CFS has an underlying biology qualitatively different from severe fatigue; an increased risk after mononucleosis is confirmed.
triangulacion: The three sources agree. The PDF conclusions speak of 'increased risk' after mononucleosis, somewhat firmer than the abstract, where the association is not statistically significant.

tema: Analyses the effects of exercise on the activation of the midbrain ascending arousal system nuclei in ME/CFS and Gulf War illness (GWI) in a PEM model.
diseno: Reanalysis of fMRI during cognitive tasks before and after submaximal exercise in 31 controls, 36 ME/CFS patients and 78 with GWI, with seed regions from the Harvard Ascending Arousal Network.
hallazgos: Before exercise, controls and GWI activated the left pedunculotegmental nucleus more than ME/CFS. After exercise, ME/CFS activated the periaqueductal grey matter, raphe nuclei, reticular formation, parabrachial complex and locus coeruleus more than GWI; controls did not change.
conclusion: Exercise had opposite effects in ME/CFS and GWI, indicating different pathophysiological mechanisms; midbrain nuclei contribute to PEM.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on midbrain, exercise and PEM; the conclusions are somewhat more cautious and present the data as an initial framework for future studies.

tema: To evaluate the effect and metabolic mechanisms of an aerobic running programme in adolescents with CFS.
diseno: Randomized trial with 46 male secondary school students with CFS (12-week intervention, 3 sessions/week of 45 min, versus control) and 24 healthy controls; nail 3-NT and urinary GC-MS.
hallazgos: The intervention reduced the fatigue score and 3-NT; differential metabolites were identified in arginine-proline, beta-alanine and pentose phosphate pathways.
conclusion: Aerobic exercise would relieve fatigue and oxidative stress, in relation to putrescine and 6-phospho-D-gluconate.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions add a recommendation of daily exercise not directly derived from the data. The CFS criteria used are not stated and the concept differs from ME/CFS with PEM.

tema: Compares the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteome of neurologic post-Lyme syndrome (nPTLS) and ME/CFS to differentiate them.
diseno: High-resolution mass spectrometry proteomics with immunoaffinity depletion and label-free quantification, in pooled and individual CSF from patients with ME/CFS (n = 43), nPTLS (n = 25) and healthy controls.
hallazgos: Both groups, and the individuals within them, were distinguished from each other and from controls by their CSF-specific proteins (p < 0.01). 2783 proteins were identified in ME/CFS, 2768 in nPTLS and 2630 in controls.
conclusion: nPTLS and ME/CFS have distinct CSF protein complements that provide candidates for validation and could lead to new diagnoses and treatments.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the CSF proteome, differential diagnosis and biomarkers. The conclusions come from the abstract itself; the pathway analysis is presented as preliminary.

tema: Analyses plasma immune signatures in ME/CFS according to disease duration.
diseno: Case-control study with analysis of plasma immune analytes; the abstract is truncated (one group of n = 246 is stated); logistic regression, classification trees with cross-validation and Spearman correlations.
hallazgos: Short-duration ME/CFS cases showed marked activation of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines and dissociation of the regulatory networks among cytokines. The alterations correlated more with duration than with severity.
conclusion: The immunopathology of ME/CFS is not static, which has implications for early diagnosis and the design of interventions.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (cytokines, duration, severity). The conclusions text corresponds to statistical methods and supplementary materials, so it provides no conclusions of its own; the abstract is incomplete.

tema: Documents the experiences of Norwegian patients with fatigue with services and interventions and compares them according to diagnostic criteria and PEM.
diseno: Online survey with respondent-driven sampling (RDS) of 660 patients; DePaul algorithms to approximate Canadian criteria (CCC) and Fukuda.
hallazgos: Most interventions were perceived as having low or negative effects; CCC patients experienced CBT, rehabilitation and work assessment programmes as more harmful; the PEM score was strongly associated with negative experiences.
conclusion: Better-designed interventions are required to avoid harm; the PEM score is useful for assessing tolerance to interventions and 'do no harm' must guide practice.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add that patients feel more understood than helped and question public investment in interventions perceived as harmful.

tema: To review the evidence for microbiome and virome alterations in ME/CFS and the methodological challenges.
diseno: Narrative review.
hallazgos: Several studies describe bacterial dysbiosis; the virome, especially bacteriophages, has been neglected; comparison between studies is difficult because of differences in criteria, processing and bioinformatics.
conclusion: Dysbiosis is evident despite contradictory results; standardized designs that include the virome are required.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions frame the microbiome within a multifactorial disease with an immune, neuroendocrine and mitochondrial interface.

tema: Maps, with a precision medicine approach, the dynamic changes in DNA methylation during a cycle of relapse and recovery in ME/CFS.
diseno: Longitudinal case study in 2 New Zealand women with ME/CFS (international consensus criteria) and 1 matched control; reduced-representation methylation sequencing at regular intervals.
hallazgos: The patients showed a 10-20 times greater methylome variability than the control. During relapse, changes in regulatory regions were associated with 157 and 127 genes, with alteration of metabolic, immune and inflammatory functions; they were different between patients but with a similarly compromised physiology.
conclusion: DNA methylation could be a signature of disease variability, useful for reducing relapses and identifying individual treatment targets.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on methylation, precision medicine and immune function. The conclusions (preprint, with medRxiv and methods noise) add the mitochondrial pathways and the variable response to drugs; the sample of two patients limits generalization.

tema: Analyses and compares autonomic and neuropathic symptoms in the post-COVID condition, ME/CFS and healthy controls, and their relationship to cognition and fatigue.
diseno: Case-control study with 87 post-COVID patients, 50 with ME/CFS and 50 controls; deep breathing, Valsalva manoeuvre and tilt-table test; Sudoscan and heat and cold evoked potentials; complete neuropsychological evaluation.
hallazgos: Heart rate was higher in ME/CFS (H = 18.3; p ≤ 0.001). POTS and pathological palmar Sudoscan values were found in 31% and 34% of ME/CFS and in 13.8% and 19.5% of post-COVID; latency to heat stimuli was longer in ME/CFS, and lower parasympathetic activation was associated with poorer cognition.
conclusion: Both syndromes are characterized by inappropriate resting tachycardia and a high prevalence of POTS; the prolonged latencies suggest damage to unmyelinated fibres and a non-length-dependent small fibre neuropathy.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions add lower cardiovagal variability in ME/CFS, not observed in post-COVID.

tema: To review alterations of lipid metabolism, energy production and oxidative stress in ME/CFS, Gulf War syndrome and fibromyalgia.
diseno: Narrative review focused on metabolomics and proteomics.
hallazgos: The three diseases share alterations in energy and lipid metabolism and oxidative stress.
conclusion: It is unclear whether these alterations are primary or secondary; energy interventions give modest benefits; the immune role, the study of PEM and of specific organs such as the brain are highlighted.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions are more cautious and broaden the focus to immune dysfunction, PEM and neuroimaging, absent from the keywords.

tema: To relate the kynurenine pathway, cytokines and plasma proteomics to ME/CFS symptoms.
diseno: Case-control with plasma measurement of kynurenine pathway metabolites, cytokines, hepcidin and proteomic screening. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Most metabolites differed; elevated kynurenine correlated with severity; lower 3-HK, 3-HAA, QUIN and PIC; hepcidin reduced by almost half; 5 of the 7 most modulated proteins related to gut health.
conclusion: The changes in the pathway would reflect inflammation and could explain fatigue and mood alterations; they require further research as biomarkers.
triangulacion: Consistent among the three sources; the conclusions add the reduction of serotonin and melatonin as a possible consequence.

tema: Doctoral thesis on how symptom and intervention heterogeneity affects the response to a cognitive-behavioural stress management (CBSM) programme in CFS.
diseno: Trial with a 10-week remote group CBSM intervention (n = 74) versus a health information control (n = 75); 5-month follow-up; fidelity analysis.
hallazgos: CBSM produced greater perceived benefit and small indirect effects on stress, depression and social disruption via stress management skills; in patients with high PEM it was associated with lower symptom frequency.
conclusion: Remote CBSM is beneficial and can be delivered by master's-level clinicians with adequate fidelity; the findings on PEM must be confirmed with a more complete evaluation.
triangulacion: There are no keywords and the abstract is only the cover page, so the information comes from the conclusions; these are cautious regarding the moderating role of PEM.

tema: Analyses whether stigma, unsupportive social interactions, symptoms and functioning are associated with depression and suicidal ideation in ME/CFS.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with patients with a self-reported diagnosis of ME or CFS; sample size not stated (90.5% met IOM criteria).
hallazgos: Those who reported suicidal ideation and depression suffered more blaming, minimization of severity and social estrangement; 7.1% reported suicidal ideation without meeting criteria for clinical depression.
conclusion: Stigma and unsupportive interactions are risk factors for suicidal ideation; this is a preliminary assessment and community psychologists should educate professionals and the public.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions are more cautious in describing the study as preliminary and noting the lack of diagnostic verification.

tema: Describes the real-world prescription of low-dose naltrexone (LDN) for pain and its perceived benefit in fibromyalgia and other chronic pain conditions.
diseno: Retrospective analysis of prescriptions at Mayo Clinic (2009-2022); 115 patients (86% women; 61% for fibromyalgia).
hallazgos: Most common dose 4.5 mg/day; 65% with follow-up reported pain benefit; adverse effects in 11% and discontinuation in 36%; concomitant analgesics, including opioids, were not associated with benefit or dropout.
conclusion: LDN is relatively safe and could benefit patients with chronic pain; no predictors were identified and a randomized controlled trial is required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the keywords do not mention ME/CFS, which does not appear as a focus of the study (centred on fibromyalgia and chronic pain).
